text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with two variants per distortion type for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: Welcome to the Bramblewick Playgroup Network volunteer training. Each session runs for 90 minutes and should include free play, a shared snack, and a story circle. Groups should never exceed twelve children per two volunteers, because smaller ratios let adults notice quiet children who might otherwise be overlooked. In 2023, volunteers reported that 64% of caregivers stayed for the whole session when songs opened the morning. Do not correct a child's drawing or tell them what colour the sky should be; instead, describe what you see and ask open questions. If a caregiver seems distressed, you are not expected to counsel them yourself. Note the concern in the session log and pass it to your hub coordinator within 48 hours.

passages.source_passage: Quarterly Monitoring Report, Kestrel Ridge Vocational Training Centre, July to September 2024. During the quarter, 146 young people enrolled across the welding, tailoring, and solar installation tracks, against a target of 160. Completion rates held steady at 81%, but placement figures were weaker. Only thirty-two graduates secured paid work within three months, and most of these came from the solar track. The tailoring cohort did not receive its planned employer visits because the partner garment workshop closed in August. Female enrolment in welding remains low, with no new women joining this quarter despite outreach at two secondary schools. Mentors reported that trainees who completed the soft-skills module were more confident in interviews than those who skipped it.

passages.source_passage: Monthly Protection Monitoring Note, Halvane Settlement, Zone C, March 2025. Case workers opened 87 new protection cases this month, of which 23 involved unaccompanied or separated children. Average time from identification to first home visit fell to four days, compared with nine days in January. Survivors of gender-based violence were referred only with documented consent, and their case files were shared with the clinic but not with camp security. However, follow-up visits were completed in Block 7 but not in Block 9, where flooding damaged the access road. Interpreters remain a bottleneck: only three staff speak Lumari, while roughly 40% of new arrivals use it as a first language. The protection desk recommends recruiting at least two additional interpreters before the rainy season peaks in May.

passages.source_passage: Background. Mbarongo District, with an estimated population of 310,000, is served by just 14 health facilities, and the nearest clinic lies more than ten kilometres from roughly half of all households. Since 2019, the Ushirika Health Trust has trained 220 community health workers to conduct household visits, screen for childhood pneumonia, and refer pregnant women for antenatal care. A 2023 review found that villages with an active health worker recorded 38% more facility deliveries than villages without one. Yet the programme has not kept pace with demand, and recruitment has stalled. Volunteers receive no regular stipend, and many leave within two years to seek paid work. Many workers leave not because the work lacks meaning but because the costs of volunteering add up.

passages.source_passage: Problem Statement. In the hill towns surrounding Corrisdale, the Larkspur Counselling Collective is the only free psychosocial service within a two-hour bus ride. A 2024 household survey commissioned by the Collective found that one in four adults reported symptoms consistent with moderate depression, yet fewer than 10% had ever spoken to a trained counsellor. Stigma remains the main barrier: many respondents said they would seek help if the centre were discreet, but not if neighbours might see them entering. Most referrals come not from clinics but from teachers and faith leaders. Our current team of six lay counsellors handles about 450 sessions a year, but the waiting list has never fallen below eighty people. Group sessions held in church halls have proven more acceptable to men, who rarely attend individual appointments.

passages.source_passage: Mid-Term Evaluation Summary, Safe Hearth Foster and Family Tracing Project, Vellmora Province. Between January 2023 and June 2024, the project placed 118 children with vetted foster families and reunified 74 with biological relatives. Evaluators found that tracing was fastest where community volunteers held local records, averaging seven weeks rather than five months. Foster carers valued the monthly support visits, though several said social workers did not arrive on schedule during the rainy season. Best-interest assessments were completed for every foster placement but not for every reunification. Follow-up after reunification was also inconsistent: only 55% of reunified children received the planned three-month check. The evaluators recommend that reunification be treated not as the end of a case but as the start of a new support phase.

passages.source_passage: Board Update, Dryland Harvest Project, Season Two. Since the October 2024 planting, 1,350 smallholder farmers in the Tessaro Valley have grown drought-tolerant sorghum and cowpea from our seed banks, up from 900 in the first season. Despite rainfall 30% below the ten-year average, participating plots yielded roughly twice as much grain as neighbouring maize fields. Not every result was positive. Seed bank committees in two villages did not return borrowed seed after harvest, though all other villages did. Farmers also told field staff that sorghum fetches lower prices than maize at local markets, so some are reluctant to expand their plots. Management does not propose abandoning the sorghum component, but we will pilot a buyer agreement with the Orrin Milling Cooperative before the March board meeting.

passages.source_passage: Background and Need. The fishing settlements along the Saltmere coast sit less than three metres above sea level, and the area has been struck by four major storm surges since 2010. During Cyclone Ferro in 2021, warning messages reached district offices six hours before landfall but did not reach most households until the wind had already risen. Sirens worked in the district town but not in the outlying villages, where loudspeakers had no backup power. Women and older people received warnings later than fishermen, since alerts were sent mainly to men's mobile phones. Evacuation drills have been held in schools but never in clinics. The Brightwater Coastal Alliance proposes to install solar-powered sirens, train volunteer warning teams in 22 villages, and test evacuation routes twice a year.

passages.source_passage: Board Update: Netwise Malaria Campaign, Lower Ombara Region. Between 3 and 21 February 2025, distribution teams delivered 64,800 long-lasting insecticidal nets to households in eleven sub-counties, reaching 92% of registered households. The campaign met its target in ten sub-counties but not in Kiraso, where heavy rains washed out two bridges and delayed trucks by almost a week. Spot checks one month later found nets hanging over sleeping spaces in 78% of visited homes, but some families were using nets to protect seedlings rather than children. Small stock losses were reported during warehouse storage but not during transport, and 1,200 nets remain in the Ombara warehouse awaiting redistribution. Management recommends that the board approve a follow-up hang-up campaign in April, focused on households with pregnant women and children under five.

passages.source_passage: Monitoring Report, Lanternlight Evening Literacy Network, Term 1, 2025. Thirty-four evening classes ran across the Pellow and Marsk districts this term, with 612 learners registered at the start and 489 still attending by week twelve. Attendance dropped sharply during the harvest fortnight, when many learners worked late in the fields. Facilitators recorded that 71% of continuing learners could now read a short public notice, compared with 29% at baseline. Classes in Pellow did not receive new primers on time, but classes in Marsk did, so only Pellow facilitators taught from handwritten charts. No learner was charged a fee, but several asked whether certificates could be issued, which the network does not currently offer. Women made up most of the enrolment, while men attended more regularly once classes moved to weekend mornings.
